editorial.title: Editorial Standards | Sarasota Flooring Company
editorial.description: How we source technical facts from NWFA, TCNA, ASTM and Florida Building Code, build 2026 installed price ranges, and correct pages when something changes.
editorial.h1: How We Research, Price and Update This Site
editorial.lede: Prices, code citations and standards on this site trace back to a named source. Here's what we check them against and how to flag something that's changed.
editorial.html:
This site publishes specific numbers (price ranges, standard references, code citations) because vague claims aren't useful when you're planning a flooring project. Here's how we build and check that information.

Where the technical facts come from

Installation methods, moisture standards, and product classifications on this site are checked against published standards and public sources: the National Wood Flooring Association (NWFA) for hardwood installation and moisture guidance, the Tile Council of North America (TCNA) for tile-setting methods, ASTM standards (including F2170 and F1869) for concrete slab moisture testing, the Florida Building Code for sound-transmission requirements between dwelling units, FEMA and NOAA for flood-zone and storm-surge information, and county and municipal permitting pages for local rules. Where we cite a specific number or standard, we name the source.

Source categories we rely on

CategoryWhat we use it for
NWFAHardwood installation, acclimation, and moisture guidance
TCNATile-setting methods and substrate requirements
ASTM (F2170, F1869)Concrete slab moisture testing methods
Florida Building CodeSound-transmission (IIC/STC) requirements between dwelling units
FEMA / NOAAFlood-zone maps and storm-surge data for barrier island and coastal jobs
County and municipal pagesLocal permitting and occupational-licensing rules
Angi, HomeAdvisor, Forbes Home, HomeGuideNational price-range context, cited with the date we pulled the figure

Where local rules vary

Some of what we cite, like condo sound-underlayment minimums, is set at the building or association level rather than by a single county-wide rule. When a page states a typical requirement, it also tells you to confirm the specific number with your condo association or property manager before you buy underlayment.

How the price ranges are built

The 2026 installed price ranges on this site, for example $1.75–$3.25 per sq ft for standard 12-mil vinyl plank or $9–$12 per sq ft for 5-inch engineered hardwood, reflect typical Sarasota and Manatee County installed costs for material and labor together, based on the range of jobs and product classes we quote in this market. They're typical ranges, not quotes: your actual number depends on the room's condition, the product you choose, and what the slab needs before flooring goes down. We label every price page with the year, and we revisit the ranges when material or labor costs shift enough to matter.

Review dates and corrections

Pages that cite prices, codes, or standards show a review date. If you find something out of date (a code citation that's changed, a price range that no longer matches what a job actually costs, a broken source link), email hello@sarasotaflooringcompany.com and we'll check it and correct the page.

AI assistance

Some of the content on this site was drafted with AI assistance and then reviewed for accuracy against the sources listed above. We don't publish an AI-generated claim about a code, a standard, or a price without checking it against a named source first; if a page states a number, a standard, or a permit rule, that fact traces back to something we verified.

Questions about a specific claim on this site, or a source we cited? Email hello@sarasotaflooringcompany.com. For a project quote instead, use the estimate form, see our about page for how we work, our workmanship warranty, or typical installed costs by material.
